articles.title: India thrash Malaysia 6-2, storm into Women's Asian Champions Trophy final - India Today
articles.summary: India thrash Malaysia 6-2, storm into Women's Asian Champions Trophy final India Today
articles.content: Defending champions India produced a commanding attacking display to defeat Malaysia 6-2 in the semi-final of the Madhya Pradesh Women's Asian Champions Trophy Bhopal 2026 at the International Sports Complex in Nathu Barkheda on Friday, and secured their place in the tournament's final for a sixth time.Tournament's top-scorer Deepika scored twice, while Mumtaz Khan, Navneet Kaur, Sunelita Toppo and Ishika found the mark once each as the hosts showcased the depth and variety of their attacking resources. Malaysia, meanwhile, showed some fight with Nur Azhar and Nuramirah Shakirah Zulkifli producing moments of individual brilliance to score two goals for their team, but it was in vain.India began on the front foot, pressed high and sought to establish control through measured midfield circulation. Malaysia, however, displayed a very good positional discipline along the right flank with defensive interventions to disrupt India's forward movements.As the opening quarter progressed, India began to find greater penetration in the attacking third, with Sunelita earning a penalty corner. Although Deepika's initial effort did not yield a direct conversion, Sunelita reacted intelligently and allowed Mumtaz to find a close-range finish and put India ahead in the 10th minute.The second quarter witnessed a decisive surge in India's attacking intensity. Navneet doubled the advantage in the 18th minute with an accomplished individual effort by taking on two Malaysian defenders before beating the goalkeeper. Hockey India PhotoThe hosts continued to stretch the Malaysian defence through incisive stick-work and combinations in the final third. Deepika then converted a penalty corner in the 25th minute into the bottom-left corner of the post to extend India's lead. Malaysia responded through Nur Azhar, who scored off a penalty corner in the 27th minute, but India swiftly reasserted their authority. Deepika struck again from a penalty corner in the 30th minute to restore India's three-goal cushion for a 4-1 lead at half-time.India carried their momentum into the third quarter with Sunelita extending the lead to 5-1 in the 33rd minute. Following Deepika's penalty-corner attempt, Sunelita reacted sharply to the rebound. Her initial effort was saved, but she remained alert to the loose ball and lifted it past the goalkeeper.India continued to dictate midfield exchanges with Lalremsiami contributing effectively to their circulation and transitions into attack. Ishika came close to producing a spectacular individual goal with an impressive solo run but failed to produce the finishing touch.India maintained their attacking intent in the final quarter. Malaysia, however, produced an individual moment of brilliance when Zulkifli unleashed a superb reverse-stick effort from the left side to score in the 52nd minute. The goal offered the visitors a measure of encouragement, but India remained composed and continued to seek openings.Rutuja Dadaso Pisal remained influential in India's attacking movements and earned another penalty corner in the 57th minute. From the ensuing set-piece, Ishika found the net. Keeping the move alive near the baseline, she maintained possession before converting it into a goal to give his team a 6-2 lead.Earlier in the day, Korea defeated Thailand 4-1 to finish fifth, while China edged past Japan 1-0 in the first semi-final, with Zhang Heyang scoring the decisive goal in the 60th minute. India will now face China in Saturday's final where the hosts and defending champions will seek a fourth Women's Asian Champions Trophy title and bring their impressive campaign to a triumphant conclusion.- EndsMust Watch

articles.title: Abhijeet Dipke: Maharashtra drought relief for farmers is less than dog upkeep - Deccan Herald
articles.summary: Abhijeet Dipke: Maharashtra drought relief for farmers is less than dog upkeep Deccan Herald
articles.content: Yavatmal: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leader Abhijeet Dipke on Thursday said the Maharashtra government has offered only Rs 5,000 to drought-stricken farmers while ministers spend more money on their dogs. . He also said that all political parties that are serious about women's reservation should field 50 per cent women candidates in upcoming State Assembly elections. . Dipke and CJP co-convenor Ashutosh Ranka visited Yavatmal district to understand farmers' distress in Vidarbha and Marathwada regions. .85% of Maharashtra declared drought-hit, farmers to get Rs 5,000 aid before Diwali: CM Fadnavis. "After listening to farmers, I realise how insensitive the government is. They are saying that they pay insurance premiums, but do not receive insurance money," Dipke said. . Some farmers had not even received the Rs 5,000 assistance announced by Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis during Diwali, he claimed. . "What will Rs 5,000 do for a farmer? All these ministers, MLAs and MPs spend more than Rs 5,000 on their dogs and they give farmers only Rs 5,000? They are insulting farmers... And for how many more months are they supposed to manage with this Rs 5,000?" Dipke asked. . Some farmers told him that they would not even have food after a month or two, the CJP leader said. . "Show a little sensitivity. At least treat them as human beings. You spend so much on your dogs, and you give farmers even less money than that. We are living in 2026," Dipke said. . When Maharashtra had a terrible drought in 1972, science had not advanced so much and India had less resources. But now in spite of scientific progress and innovation, farmers are still at the mercy of nature, he said. . "If nature does not cooperate, should farmers commit suicide?.....If farmers are supposed to remain completely dependent on nature, then why do we elect a government?" Dipke said. . To a question on the women's reservation bill, he asked why the quota for women should remain limited to 33 per cent. As women account for half the population, political parties should give 50 percent of tickets to women in the upcoming elections, he said. . "Give tickets to women in Uttar Pradesh, Punjab and Uttarakhand. All parties that are serious and sincere about women’s reservation should give tickets to women first. How many women are there in your cabinet? Just one, and you talk about women’s representation?" Dipke said.

articles.title: New Zealand’s Tom Blundell opens up on difficulty of being one-format player - The Indian Express
articles.summary: New Zealand’s Tom Blundell opens up on difficulty of being one-format player The Indian Express
articles.content: New Zealand batter Tom Blundell opened up on the difficulty of being a one-format player after staying unbeaten on 53 at the end of the opening day's play of the second India vs New Zealand Test match. The Kiwi player last played a T20I in 2024, while he hasn't appeared in an ODI since 2023. "I look back to last season and domestic cricket. I had probably one of my best seasons throughout the formats in domestic cricket. At times I do find it hard just being a one-format cricketer. You go through periods where you might not play Test cricket for three or four months and then all of a sudden you're playing Test cricket in India," he said. "So it can be quite challenging at times, but I feel my game's in a really good spot. It just needs a bit of game time, and that was nice today to be able to spend, you know, time out there and get a bit of the rhythm back, I guess," he added. The batter also said he is happy with the 246/5 that his team managed and the "big job" now is to take it past 300 on the challenging track that's "nipping quite a lot". "It was a little bit slow from all counts initially, but yeah throughout the whole day, it was nipping quite a lot. (we will) take it 100 per cent. I'm pretty happy," he said. "If you look at it tomorrow, me and Glenn have got a big job if we can carry on that partnership and get us above 300, and 300-plus would be ideal. But the Indian bowlers, they bowled pretty well all day. It's pretty tough out there facing all of them with that nipping ball, but I thought, you know, all of them bowled really well," he added.

I had probably one of my best seasons throughout the formats in domestic cricket. At times I do find it hard just being a one-format cricketer. You go through periods where you might not play Test cricket for three or four months and then all of a sudden you're playing Test cricket in India," he said. "So it can be quite challenging at times, but I feel my game's in a really good spot. It just needs a bit of game time, and that was nice today to be able to spend, you know, time out there and get a bit of the rhythm back, I guess," he added. The batter also said he is happy with the 246/5 that his team managed and the "big job" now is to take it past 300 on the challenging track that's "nipping quite a lot". "It was a little bit slow from all counts initially, but yeah throughout the whole day, it was nipping quite a lot. (we will) take it 100 per cent. I'm pretty happy," he said. "If you look at it tomorrow, me and Glenn have got a big job if we can carry on that partnership and get us above 300, and 300-plus would be ideal. But the Indian bowlers, they bowled pretty well all day. It's pretty tough out there facing all of them with that nipping ball, but I thought, you know, all of them bowled really well," he added.

India 3:39.97. - Team Sportstar Bihar State Games 2026: Around 5,500 athletes to compete across 24 disciplines Around 5,500 athletes from across Bihar will compete in 24 sporting disciplines at the Bihar State Games 2026, scheduled to be held in Patna and Rajgir from December 1 to 10, an official statement said on Friday. Chief Secretary Pratyay Amrit chaired a meeting to review preparations for the Games, directing various government departments and the Patna and Nalanda district administrations to ensure the smooth conduct of the event. The opening ceremony will be held at Gandhi Maidan in Patna. According to a statement issued by the Cabinet Secretariat, around 750 technical officials and an equal number of volunteers will be involved in the 10-day event. Competitions in Patna will take place at the Pataliputra Sports Complex in Kankarbagh, the Sports Building-cum-Gymnasium in Rajendra Nagar, Ganga Path (Marine Drive), Secretariat Sports Club, Bikram Shooting Range and Young Men’s Institute. The State Sports Academy in Rajgir and the Kalyan Bigha Shooting Range will host events in Nalanda district. Amrit instructed the Home Department, police authorities and district administrations to make adequate security arrangements at competition venues, accommodation facilities and the opening ceremony. The Patna traffic police was asked to formulate a special traffic management plan to facilitate the movement of athletes and officials. The Health Department has been tasked with deploying medical teams and ambulances, besides ensuring the availability of essential medicines and other medical facilities. Arrangements will also be made for safe drinking water at venues and accommodation facilities. The Urban Development and Housing Department has been directed to oversee sanitation, street lighting, road repairs and maintenance of public facilities. The Education Department, Bihar State Sports Authority and State Sports Academy have been asked to coordinate the participation of athletes, coaches and technical officials and ensure the availability of equipment across all 24 disciplines. - PTI GYMNASTICS Prasad Salap’s four-gold flourish powers Maharashtra’s triumph at Youth Gymnastics Champs Maharashtra and Uttar Pradesh continued their impressive medal-winning spree at the 1st Youth Artistic Gymnastics National Championships, stamping their authority on Day 3 by clinching the Grade 9 Out-Age and In-Age team titles, respectively, at INS Hamla, Malad. Maharashtra produced a commanding display of precision, power and consistency to top the Grade 9 Out-Age team standings with 177.400 points. Uttar Pradesh put up a spirited challenge to finish runners-up with 173.199, while West Bengal secured third place with 154.035. Maharashtra’s Prasad Santosh Salap was the standout performer in the Out-Age category, combining technical finesse with remarkable execution to capture the individual all-around crown with 63.633 points. His teammate Aadesh Waghchoude delivered a strong performance to finish second with 61.501, while Services’ Ayush Nath claimed third place with 60.900. Prasad further underlined his dominance in the apparatus finals, displaying exceptional control, strength and composure to sweep four gold medals. He topped the Pommel Horse, Still Rings, Parallel Bars and Horizontal Bar events, showcasing his versatility across the apparatus. Haryana’s Ritik impressed with his floor routine to claim the Floor Exercise title, while Services’ Tushar Khanra emerged victorious in the Vault. In the Grade 9 In-Age competition, Uttar Pradesh produced an equally impressive team performance, accumulating 194.533 points to secure the championship. Services finished a close second with 185.466, narrowly edging Odisha (GFI-2), who finished third with 185.366. Maharashtra’s Jeet Santosh Chavan delivered a polished all-around performance, blending fluid transitions, assured landings and technical precision to clinch the individual title with an impressive 67.034 points. Uttar Pradesh’s Yatharth Kesharwani finished second with 65.634, while his teammate Kush secured third place with 65.533 in a closely contested battle. Jeet continued his golden run in the apparatus finals, displaying excellent rhythm and control to capture the Floor Exercise and Pommel Horse titles. Yatharth showcased his strength and execution to top the Still Rings and Horizontal Bar, while Uttar Pradesh’s Ujjwal Kumar Pandit produced a commanding Parallel Bars routine to claim gold. Karnataka’s Sai Daksh Mohan Kadam rounded off the apparatus champions by topping the Vault. - Team Sportstar TENNIS ITF Kolkata W15: Jensi stuns fourth seed Pankratova to enter semifinals Talented teenager Jensi Dipakbhai Kanabar stunned fourth seed Maria Pankratova 7-6(4), 6-2 to storm into the singles semifinals of the women’s ITF tournament in Kolkata on Friday. The 14-year-old Jensi recovered from a 3-5 deficit in the opening set to force a tie-break, where she overturned a 1-4 deficit to take the set against the Russian 20-year-old. After both players traded breaks, Pankratova appeared to be in control of the tie-break after racing to a 4-1 lead. articles.title: Maharashtra makes promotions primary route for senior posts in Government Medical Colleges - Medical Dialogues
articles.summary: Maharashtra makes promotions primary route for senior posts in Government Medical Colleges Medical Dialogues
articles.content: Mumbai: The Maharashtra government has made promotions the primary route for filling senior academic and administrative positions in government medical colleges, narrowing opportunities for candidates from outside the state-run medical education system.Under the revised recruitment rules notified by the Medical Education Department, associate professors with a minimum of three years of experience in their respective subjects will be eligible for promotion to the post of professor. The eligibility criteria for the post of dean have also been tightened. Candidates must have served as professors in government medical colleges for at least five years and possess a minimum of 10 years of teaching experience in a medical institution.Also Read:11 contractual doctors allegedly paid bribes for permanent jobs at Pune Medical College, complaint filedSimilarly, appointments to the post of joint director will be made through promotion. Selection will be based on seniority among deans who have completed at least three years in the position.The revised framework retains a combination of promotion and direct recruitment for associate professor vacancies. Half of these posts will be filled through promotions, while the remaining 50 per cent will be filled through direct recruitment based on recommendations of the Maharashtra Public Service Commission (MPSC), BW Education reported. Recruitment to assistant professor positions will continue to take place through direct selection by the commission.The changes have raised concerns over the limited opportunities for experienced medical educators and researchers working outside government medical colleges to enter the state's senior academic and administrative hierarchy.Critics have also questioned the increased reliance on seniority for leadership appointments, arguing that the approach could restrict the entry of candidates with substantial academic, research and institutional experience.The revised rules are expected to reshape career progression within Maharashtra's government medical colleges, particularly for faculty aspiring to move into senior teaching and administrative positions. They also mark a shift towards an internal promotion-based system for filling key leadership posts in the state's medical education department.Also Read:MP medical teachers announce statewide agitation on December 14 over 12-point demands

articles.title: India’s 2036 Olympic pitch faces IOC question: Can it become a multi-sport nation? - The Indian Express
articles.summary: India’s 2036 Olympic pitch faces IOC question: Can it become a multi-sport nation? The Indian Express
articles.content: India’s delegation escaped awkward questions on the country’s troubled sports governance and doping record, but the International Olympic Committee’s (IOC's) Future Hosts Commission did have one question for the team pitching the 2036 Olympic bid: How does India move beyond being a single-sport nation? The question was not about India’s Olympic medal tally – two gold medals since the turn of the century and six medals overall at Paris 2024 – but about how the country plans to broaden its sporting base in a landscape dominated by cricket. The 10-member Indian delegation - led by union sports minister Mansukh Mandaviya and comprising IOC member Nita Ambani and Gujarat's deputy chief minister Harsh Sanghavi, among others - pointed to the two athletes in the room as examples: former athlete PT Usha, the outgoing Indian Olympic Association president, and shuttler PV Sindhu. “Our answer was that we have heroes like PT Usha and PV (Sindhu), who have played key roles in revolutionising athletics and badminton in the country. Once you create a hero, the fan following builds and people take up the sport,” IOC chief executive Raghuram Iyer, who was a part of the presentation team, told The Indian Express. “We also explained to the Commission how all stakeholders are together putting structures in place for all the other leagues that are coming up in various sports. The role of the Khelo India programme for grassroots development was also highlighted.” The Indian delegation’s virtual presentation to the Future Hosts Commission on Thursday focused largely on the technical aspects of the proposed 2036 Olympic Games bid, with infrastructure, funding and the venue masterplan forming the bulk of the discussions. The Commission is headed by former Croatia president Kolinda Grabar-Kitarovic and has eight other members. The presentation lasted around 25 minutes, followed by a question-and-answer session and a further 20 minutes of interaction with the Commission. “The presentation was very good. It was cordial and nice. They asked pertinent questions," Iyer said after the meeting. India is among seven National Olympic Committees currently in the IOC’s continuous dialogue phase for the 2036 Games. The others are Germany, Hungary, Qatar, South Korea, South Africa and Turkey. Elephant in the room Although the Commission didn't raise the issue, the Indian delegation also addressed the doping menace, with India recording the most anti-doping rule violations, according to the World Anti-Doping Agency. “We spoke about the efforts undertaken by the National Anti-Doping Agency and the National Anti-Doping Act as strict measures to curb the menace,” Iyer said. The discussion, however, was largely centred on India’s preparedness to host the Games, particularly its infrastructure plans. India highlighted the upcoming 2030 Commonwealth Games as an important stepping stone towards possibly hosting the Olympics six years later. The delegation told the Commission that venues being developed for the CWG would also be used for the Olympics. India’s proposed venue masterplan is spread across seven clusters, with Ahmedabad and Gandhinagar forming the centrepiece. The Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel Sports Enclave in Ahmedabad’s Motera area is expected to be a key hub, with the proposed Olympic Village and several sporting venues forming part of the wider development plan. The masterplan envisages a concentration of venues around Ahmedabad and Gandhinagar, with the possibility of using existing sporting infrastructure in other cities for select events. Previous plans have identified venues in centres such as Mumbai, Pune, Bhopal and Goa for disciplines that can be held outside Gujarat. The Paralympic Games and accessibility of infrastructure also came up during the discussion. The delegation was asked how the proposed venues and supporting facilities would cater to athletes with disabilities. “We highlighted how the Olympics and Paralympics will improve accessibility in the city, which will hugely benefit the wider population,” Iyer said. The next major milestone in the selection process is expected in March 2027, when the IOC will complete its feasibility assessments and the Executive Board will decide which interested parties advance to the Strategic Dialogue phase. Those shortlisted will undergo a more detailed evaluation, including site visits by the Future Hosts Commission and scrutiny of their venue plans, funding strategies and other guarantees. The IOC is expected to open a Targeted Dialogue with its preferred hosts in December 2028, before the host of the 2036 Olympics is elected by IOC members in mid-2029.
